questions.q: What is a Log Analytics workspace?
options: A real Azure Monitor resource that stores log and telemetry data, used across Azure and not exclusive to Sentinel
A feature that only exists inside the Sentinel product itself
A local file on an analyst's own computer
A third-party tool unrelated to Azure
questions.explain: The Log Analytics workspace is a real Azure Monitor Logs resource, used for log/telemetry storage across Azure, not just by Sentinel.

questions.q: When you 'enable Sentinel' on a workspace, what is actually happening?
options: Sentinel's security capabilities are turned on on top of an existing (or newly created) Log Analytics workspace
A brand-new, separate database is created that has nothing to do with Log Analytics
The workspace is deleted and replaced by Sentinel's own storage
Nothing changes in Azure at all
questions.explain: Sentinel doesn't bring its own separate data store — it activates on top of a Log Analytics workspace that holds the actual data.

questions.q: Why is Sentinel best described as 'a security UI layer on top of Log Analytics' rather than a separate database?
options: Because every log Sentinel shows is actually a row in a table inside the same underlying Log Analytics workspace
Because Sentinel and Log Analytics have no relationship to each other
Because Sentinel stores a duplicate copy of all data in its own private store
Because Log Analytics is a feature inside Sentinel, not the other way around
questions.explain: Sentinel's incident queue, rules, and hunting pages all read from and write to the same workspace tables — there's no separate Sentinel data store.

questions.q: Which of these is a real, named table inside a Log Analytics workspace, as covered in this lesson?
options: SigninLogs, for Entra ID sign-in events
SentinelMasterTable, a single table holding all data types
DefenderOnly, a table exclusive to antivirus alerts
NoSQLBlob, an unstructured catch-all table
questions.explain: SigninLogs, SecurityEvent, OfficeActivity, and CommonSecurityLog are real named tables data connectors write into.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what three things are governed at the Log Analytics workspace level?
options: Where KQL queries run, access control via Azure RBAC, and cost/retention
Only the color scheme of the Sentinel user interface
Nothing — all of these are configured per individual analytics rule instead
Only which playbooks are allowed to run
questions.explain: KQL queries run directly against the workspace, Azure RBAC governs access at the workspace level, and cost/retention are billed per workspace.
